sources.title: Improved lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles
sources.snippet: The Shannon capacity $Θ(G)$ of a graph $G$ quantifies the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted with zero error over a noisy channel. It is lower bounded by $α(G^d)^{1/d}$ for any $d$, where $α(G^d)$ is the independence number of the $d$-th strong product of $G$. We construct independent sets of size $134753$ in $C_7^{10}$, $21909$ in $C_{11}^{6}$, $62530$ in $C_{13}^{6}$, and $8076974$ in $C_{15}^{8}$, improving the best known lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of these graphs

sources.title: Leaking Information Through Cache LRU States
sources.snippet: The Least-Recently Used cache replacement policy and its variants are widely deployed in modern processors. This paper shows for the first time in detail that the LRU states of caches can be used to leak information: any access to a cache by a sender will modify the LRU state, and the receiver is able to observe this through a timing measurement. sources.title: Multi-step LRU: SIMD-based Cache Replacement for Lower Overhead and Higher Precision
sources.snippet: A key-value cache is a key component of many services to provide low-latency and high-throughput data accesses to a huge amount of data.
